tasks.title: Consolidate Geofabrik extraction while preserving world-provider workflows
tasks.notes: OWNER DECISION AND IMPLEMENTATION REQUEST 2026-11-21: consolidate extraction in shared tool code, with a small world-local wrapper supplying regional configuration and deliberate overrides. Implement in an agent on a dedicated worktree. Capture and preserve Southampton's current CLI options, output filenames, combined GeoJSON and evidence-manifest registration; the current shared extractor is not a drop-in replacement. Move useful portable capabilities into shared code with regional settings supplied as configuration, and keep standard queries in one place. Every GDAL extraction must explicitly supply OSM_CONFIG_FILE, honour deliberate local schema overrides and fall back to the shared schema. Replace the world duplicate only after compatibility is covered; preserve owner edits. Meaningful temporary-fixture/subprocess-double checks must cover furniture/schema arguments, both entry points, legacy options and outputs, manifest registration and preservation of previous good outputs on failure. Tool tests must use synthetic providers, never import the live world's implementation. A separate small change belongs in the world repository for its wrapper. No live block writes, downloads or remote writes are part of this implementation request. Original report: the world extractor omitted OSM_CONFIG_FILE and GDAL's default schema lacked the amenity column used by furniture queries, blocking prepare. A local patch selected world downloads/osmconf.ini or TOOL_ROOT/config/osmconf.ini; inspect the current file because that historical patch may now be committed. Original prepare manifest hints for prepared-53--42, prepared-54--42, 52,-42 and 52,-43 were not run; do not retroactively register those as part of this refactor.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Woodland: dense fill, mixed species, understorey and woodland floor
tasks.notes: Deliverable: inside wood polygons, fill towards the aerial canopy cover (about 80%), mixed species and heights, understorey bushes (persistent leaves at Y+1 to Y+2) and ferns, podzol/coarse_dirt/moss_block floor with grass at the edges; labelled inference, removable through the foliage and decor masks. Owner: trees need more density. Performance evidence clarified 2026-11-21 (read-only): the trial quotes 962 s for 113 trees, but 8.5 s per tree is only an average of the reported total, not a measured per-tree bottleneck. The saved farmland trees-result.json (journal_seq 1292) records 17,915 positions, writer total 2.35 s, and 40.38 s summed across recorded apply stages; planning before site_kit.apply is not included in that result. The code already batches tree writes into one cell plan. The cause of the remainder of the reported command time is not established; profile planning and full command stages before choosing an optimisation or projecting dense-woodland cost. The earlier live-planning cache-thrash/low-probe-floor problem has a landed fix in #315 (planning from saved regions); distinguish it from the still-unexplained 962 s total. Numeric runtime limit remains to be agreed. Check: wood across the river in cell 63,-45 matches the aerial density; apply time for it stays under a stated limit; owner verdict in game. Profile 2026-11-21 (read-only dry run of trees_layer on 87,-48 under cProfile, current code with #315): 85 s total. planning_inputs 52.9 s, of which neighbour_owned 36 s (cell_journal._cell_owners rebuilds ownership per cell, uncacheable because builds are excluded; about 9 million block_id calls; scales with journal history, not tree count); dry site_kit.apply 16.9 s; surface warm-up 5.6 s; plan_cell (tree placement) 5.7 s. Dry run planted 51 trees and 10,306 blocks, not the trial's 113 trees and 17,915 positions, so it is indicative only. Current planning is about a minute, so the 962 s is not explained by planning on current code: it was pre-#315 live planning or the live apply stages (MCP write and readback), which a dry run cannot show. Next: time a live apply with the existing timed_stage output; the ownership lookup is a candidate optimisation. Live apply 2026-11-21 (87,-48, after prepare --apply cleared a stale readiness validation): 77 s wall, but NOT a clean redo and NOT the 113-tree workload. The apply did not undo the earlier trees pass (the dry run simulates that undo, apply_cell does not), so 51 crowns were skipped as trunk blocked and only 3 trees (556 blocks) were planted on top. Stages: layer planning 38.6 s, identity and readiness 4.1 s, journal begin 6.1 s, writer total 12.7 s (player hop 9.3 s), flush 3.6 s, readback 0.4 s. Side effect, owner chose not to repair: the trees mask for 87,-48 now holds 556 positions instead of the 17,915 of journal #1292, so the original trees remain in the world but are outside the mask (mask-based undo or redo would only touch the 3 new trees). A real full-workload timing needs undo then apply of the trees pass, on a cell where that is acceptable. Ghost frontier finding 2026-11-21 (ground apply on 46,-46, run from prepare then ground): the apply took 984 s and 883 s of it was the 'journal follow-ups' stage (registry.ensure writing 7 frontier ghost cells, journal #1656-1668, about 126 s and 1.1 million planned blocks per cell); every other stage summed to about 100 s. Owner decision: the ghost frontier is wanted and stays; it must be completed before a timing starts, so measure applies on cells whose frontier already exists (the follow-ups stage then takes about 0 s, as on 87,-48). This does not explain the trial's 962 s: the 87,-48 trees apply (#1292) had no ghost builds after it. Still open: a full-workload trees timing needs an open-land cell with no planned features and a valid readiness check; 46,-46 is blocked by the planned houses_burgess_road feature (must land before trees/decor) and a stale validation (#232). Full-workload trees timing 2026-11-21 (46,-46 after the houses landed and a ground redo, frontier already complete so journal follow-ups took 0.003 s; existing planner, 256 crowns, 41,160 blocks, readback 0 mismatches): about 100 s of stage time. layer planning 54.2 s; registry.begin guard reads and journal write 14.0 s; surface warm-up in apply 9.8 s; readback 8.6 s; identity and readiness 3.9 s; flush 3.3 s; writer 2.6 s; backup 1.0 s. Placement is not the cost, and the trial 962 s is still unexplained (likely before #315 and #343, or a pending frontier). A runtime limit of a few minutes looks reachable; the numeric limit is still to be agreed. Dry-run cProfile of planning (inflated by the profiler): _box about 24 s, aerial tile decoding about 14 s, lidar about 7 s, neighbour_owned about 6.6 s, plan_cell about 6 s. Filed #345 for the box filter and decode caching; not filed: profiling registry.begin and the apply warm-up, and timing ground and decor. The earlier open blockers (planned house feature, stale validation) are cleared on 46,-46. Owner feedback on the existing planner, filed as issue I-055 (held until #318): too sparse versus the aerial (dense wood with a few clearings), grass floor where podzol and ground cover belong, and no species variety. Runtime limit agreed 2026-11-21: 8 minutes for a tree build; flag at 8, kill at 12 (150%), continue to the next cell in long runs, and report every 8+ minute tree build at the end of the run. The watchdog and reporting are filed as a separate task (see the task list entry Run budget for long runs). What #318 still needs: the woodland design work (diagnose why the existing cover-based fill is still sparse; species mix; understorey; podzol/moss/fern floor) and the 63,-45 check. Proving cells agreed 2026-11-21: both 63,-45 (the wood across the river; validation stale, needs prepare --apply) and 46,-46 (small wood beside the Burgess Road houses; existing planner already applied, owner snags I-055 filed against it). The check is the woodland density matching the aerial, the apply under the 8 minute budget, and the owner verdict in game, on both.

tasks.title: Speed up trees planning: box filter and aerial decode caching
tasks.notes:
Found while timing #318 (trees on 46,-46, 2026-11-21): the live trees apply spends 54 s in "layer planning", more than half of its ~100 s of stage time. A dry-run cProfile (inflated by the profiler, 86 s total) put planning_inputs at 57 s: _box in lib/layers/trees_layer.py about 24 s; aerial tile decoding about 14 s (aerial_coverage.require_coverage and samples appear to decode the same tiles more than once); lidar reads about 7 s; neighbour_owned about 6.6 s; plan_cell about 6 s. Placement and writing are already cheap.

Scope, in order:
1. _box (mean over a k x k window, edge padded) adds k*k shifted copies of the whole 4608x4352 mosaic; with k=35 that is 1225 full-image adds. Replace it with a separable running-sum (numpy only; scipy is not installed). Output must match the old one: the callers threshold it (>0.5, >0.999, >1e-6, sd >= 0.035).
2. Cache aerial tile decodes within a run so require_coverage, samples and the canopy/cover detectors do not re-decode the same tile. Check first that the repeats are real duplicates.

Acceptance, synthetic only: a test comparing the old _box (keep as a test oracle) with the new one on random and edge-heavy arrays for k = 5, 7, 9, 35, including the thresholded masks being equal; canopy_pixels and cover_pixels give identical masks on a synthetic image; the decode cache returns identical arrays. No world build step in this task, so requiresClaude is false.

Out of scope: any change to crown selection, placement or thresholds. Real-cell check is done by the orchestrator after merge, not by the worker: trees dry run on 46,-46 before and after must give the same 256 crowns and 41,160 blocks (before: dry run 2026-11-21, report highfield_46_m46_trees-dry-report.json), then record the new planning time on #318. Target: planning about 54 s to about 30 s with step 1, about 20 s with step 2.

Not a stretch: output unchanged, no schema, journal or cross-layer geometry change. A cheaper model than the orchestrator is fine. Related: #318 (timing), #343 (ownership lookup speed-up, done).

tasks.title: Run budget for long runs: flag at budget, kill at 150%, continue to next cell
tasks.notes:
Owner decision 2026-11-21 (from #318 timing work): a tree build has a runtime budget of 8 minutes. In a long (unattended) run, a build that reaches the budget is flagged; it is killed at 150% of the budget (12 minutes); the run then goes on to the next cell instead of stopping. At the end of the run the report lists every tree build that took 8 minutes or more, whether it finished or was killed.

Today lib/site/site_lock.py run() starts the command in its own session and handles SIGTERM (then SIGKILL) but has no deadline, and nothing records how long a build took. Scope:
1. site_lock.py run (and the CLI) gets a budget: --budget-min N (flag at N) and --kill-factor F (default 1.5). At the budget it prints one OVER-BUDGET line with owner, task and elapsed; at N*F it kills the process group the way run() already does (SIGTERM, short grace, SIGKILL), releases the lock as it always does, and exits with a distinct status (for example 124), different from an ordinary failure. Without --budget-min nothing changes.
2. Every run that finishes or is killed writes its elapsed time and verdict (ok, over-budget, killed) to a machine-readable record that site_status.py morning can read, so the end-of-run report lists builds of 8 minutes or more with cell, elapsed and verdict.
3. cell-orchestrator skill (overnight mode): trees builds run with --budget-min 8; exit 124 is a killed build, not a failure: run site_recover.py status/recover for that cell (existing rule), log a PROBLEM with the elapsed time, exclude the cell for this run, and continue. A killed build does not count toward the two-consecutive-failures stop and is not retried. The repeated-tool-error stop still applies to other causes. The morning summary lists the over-budget builds.

Acceptance, synthetic only: tests run a harmless sleeping command with a tiny budget (seconds) and check the flag line, the kill, the exit status, that the lock is released, that the record is written, and that a run under budget is untouched. No world build step in this task, so requiresClaude is false. The orchestrator-skill wording is covered by the skill-stub test. Other layers have no budget yet (ground redo on 46,-46 took about 3 minutes plus a possible frontier of about 2 minutes per new cell edge); set them once timed.

Related: #318 (timing and the 8 minute budget), #345 (speeds trees planning).
